I will also create an SVG pouch design.</p><p>Six more premium images are planned. These include a dry fruit flatlay on marble, a bright kitchen lifestyle shot, and a hands-pouring oats photo. The total will be six high-quality images.</p><p>The hero product is a cream stand-up pouch with a zipper seal. It will feature bold "nutri" and gold "Rx" text, a leaf badge, and illustrated nuts on the right. The front will show "OAT" in dark brown and "MY GOODNESS" in gold. The back will list premium ingredients, an Urdu line, and badges for HALAL, protein, fiber, and no preservatives. The net weight will read 500 grams.</p><p>I will generate the product image and the SVG pouch in parallel. The SVG will serve as the primary visual to avoid fake photography. I am also sketching the full design system and page structure before writing any code.</p><p>The brand will be displayed as "nutriRx" with "NutriRx" in body text. The product name will be "OAT ‚Äî My Goodness" with "OATs" noted as the common abbreviation. The site will have a home page for marketing and an order page for checkout.</p><p>The site will also include a success page with order tracking and a review form. A separate track page will let customers look up their order status. An admin dashboard will handle order management. The API will support order creation, status updates, admin authentication, reviews, and newsletter subscriptions. The database will store orders, reviews, and subscribers.</p><p>Order status will be stored simply with an updated timestamp. Admin statistics will use query aggregates. Pakistan-specific details are being added: PKR formatting, local phone placeholders, city lists, COD as the main payment method, and a prominent Urdu language toggle. Delivery estimates will be two to five working days. WhatsApp is unavailable, so orders will be confirmed by phone. Instagram embeds are not possible without API access.</p><p>A styled link card will direct visitors to the Instagram handle. Animated falling oats were considered but rejected as gimmicky. Form validation rules are being defined: names must be at least two characters, phone numbers must match a Pakistani mobile regex, city selection is required, addresses need at least eight characters, quantity is limited to one through twelve, and email is optional but validated when provided. A settings table will be added to the database so the admin can manage inventory levels.</p><p>A dedicated products table will store the Oats item with fields for slug, name, price in PKR, weight, stock, and active status. An idempotent seed function will ensure the product record exists on the first API call.</p><p>The seed function will insert the Oats product with 120 units in stock. Orders will decrement stock automatically. If stock hits zero, customers will be offered a waitlist subscription. Order statuses will run from pending through delivered or cancelled. Cancelled orders will restore stock. Admin authentication will use HMAC-signed cookies with Node crypto.</p><p>The admin cookie will not use the secure flag so it works on HTTP previews. The admin panel will use a dark espresso design that feels like a studio backroom rather than generic Bootstrap. The homepage will be built as a single large client component called <code class="rounded bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-sm" data-streamdown="inline-code">HomeExperience</code> with smaller sub-components to keep files manageable. I am also planning the core file structure, starting with the database schema, a catalog library for constants and city lists, a formatting utility, and an orders module for code generation and pricing.</p><p>A newsletter subscription API route is being added. The layout will use a client-side provider to wrap children for language context. A bilingual copy dictionary will store English and Urdu text.</p><p>I have chosen Noto Nastaliq Urdu as the primary font for Urdu text. It is authentic and premium for Pakistani branding. They considered adding a free-delivery threshold for orders of two or more items, but decided against inventing delivery fees since the owner only specified the product price.
